title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and Computed Tomography (CT) of the Spine - Medical Clinical Policy Bulletins | Aetna

criteria.description: Cauda equina syndrome documented (e.g., saddle anesthesia, bowel/bladder dysfunction, progressive lower extremity weakness)
Suspected spinal malignancy documented (e.g., known cancer with new spinal symptoms, imaging findings suggestive of metastasis, or ICD-10 codes C41.2, C70.1, C72.0-C72.1, C79.51-C79.52)

Suspected spinal infection documented (e.g., osteomyelitis, discitis, epidural abscess, tuberculosis of spine; ICD-10 codes A18.01, A18.03, G06.1, M46.20-M46.39, M86.08, M86.18, M86.28, M86.38, M86.48, M86.58, M86.68, M86.8x8, M86.9, M89.68, M90.88)
Acute lumbar spine fracture, dislocation, or significant trauma documented (ICD-10 codes S32.000A-S32.2xxS, S33.100A-S33.39xS)

Progressive neurological deficit documented (e.g., worsening radiculopathy, myelopathy, or new/worsening motor/sensory loss; ICD-10 codes M50.00-M50.03, M51.04-M51.06, M50.10-M50.13, M50.20-M50.23, M51.24-M51.27)
Low back pain duration of 6 weeks or more documented

Conservative therapy (moderate activity, analgesics, NSAIDs, muscle relaxants) completed for adequate duration without improvement; symptoms persist, worsen, or do not improve despite conservative care
Neurological examination performed and documented (assessment of motor, sensory, reflexes, straight leg raise) to evaluate for radiculopathy or neurologic deficit
